neighbours.label: an unwanted public image or reputation being described: the slot around the unflattering quality in 'shed/shake its … image/reputation' and 'wants to be seen as …' (the + pole takes attribution verbs: credited, counts as, accuse)
fire: Years after the scandal, the bank has never really shed its greedy public image.
No governor wants to be seen as soft on corruption.
The neighbourhood is still trying to shake its violent reputation.
The sport has struggled to lose its elitist image among working families.
No manager wants to be viewed as indecisive in a crisis.
The town has never quite escaped its backward reputation.
The industry has worked hard to shed its dirty image.
No candidate wants to be perceived as arrogant by the voters.
quiet: Years after the scandal, the bank has never really recovered its lost deposits.
The governor signed the anti-corruption bill on Tuesday.
The neighbourhood is still trying to repair its broken streetlights.
The sport has struggled to attract working families to its clubs.
The manager decided to wait until the crisis had passed.
The town has never quite finished its new library.
The industry has worked hard to cut its emissions.
The candidate spoke to the voters for almost an hour.

notes: Low confidence. Probes: 'shake its dangerous reputation' 0.46, 'wants to be seen as weak' 0.38, 'to be blamed' 0.28, 'its rebellious image' 0.23, 'its brutal public image' 0.12, 'to be labeled a traitor' 0.02, 'to be remembered as' 0.02. The card's CJK examples were not explored.
